title: SPA/302/2015 of Chandra Shekhar Arora Vs Zila Panchayat Dehradun

paras.text:
SPA No. 302 of 2015
Honíble Ravi Malimath, A.C.J.
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
 Ms. Gurbani Singh, learned counsel for
the appellant-writ petitioner.
 Shri N.S. Pundir, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
 Heard learned counsels.
 There is a delay of 432 days in filing the
Review Application. The reason assigned for
the delay is that the writ petitioner was not
aware of the order being passed and he did
not receive any communication from the
learned counsel. It is only, thereafter, when
he came to know of the same, that the instant
review application has been filed.
 On considering the reasons assigned, we
are of the view that the same constitutes
sufficient cause for condoning the delay.
Accordingly, the Delay Condonation
Application (CLMA No. 607 of 2020) is allowed
and the delay in filing the review application
is condoned.
 On considering the submissions, we do
not find any error apparent on the face of
record that calls for a review. The writ
petition has been dismissed on the ground
that the possession of the shop of the writ

petitioner, as well as vacant area adjoining the
shop, has been reserved for the purposes of a
public utility, namely, a urinal/toilet.
Therefore, the writ petitioner would not have
any right, title or interest over the said
property. The Division Bench has rightly
considered the merits while affirming the
order passed by the learned Single Judge.
 Hence, in the absence of any error
apparent on the face of record, the Review
Application (MCC No. 45 of 2020) is
dismissed.
 However, liberty is reserved to the writ
petitioner to make an application for a fresh
allotment, or otherwise, with the respondent-authorities, who would consider the same in
accordance with and in a manner known to
law.
 Pending application(s), if any, also
stands dismissed.

(Manoj K. Tiwari, J.) (Ravi Malimath, A.C.J.)
 25.09.2020 25.09.2020
R.P.
